Incident Notes: Sheep was killed, DFW confirmed that a cougar was responsible. RP was advised to fully enclose the animals at night. A cougar has been spotted on Vashon Island several times since this incident including October 22 and 23.
Calf was killed and partially consumed. DFW responded and found wounds consistent with a cougar kill as well as cougar hair caught in the fence. A depredation permit was issued.

Three goats killed near Creston. DFW and hound hunter responded. Two cougars were treed and dispatched. RP shot and wounded a third cougar around 0130 hours the next day. DFW and hound hunters responded but could not find the wounded cougar.

Two sheep were killed and partially buried. DFW Enforcement responded and set up trail cameras. Cougar returned over next couple days and took three chickens and a turkey. Cougar was tracked and euthanized. It was an adult female with injured jaw.

RP lost a sheep to a cougar. A Fish and Wildlife Officer confirmed that a cougar was responsible based on the feeding pattern of cutting through the ribs to access internal organs. RP shot the cougar the next morning when it returned.
RP advised that he had shot at a cougar that was trying to jump the fence into their dog kennel. RP was given advice.

RP advised she saw a cougar near her goat farm and was concerned it would attack her goats. A houndsman tracked the cougar, treed it, and left it unharmed. The houndsman reported seeing tracks from two other cougars.
RP heard loud sounds coming from garage, went outside, and saw a cougar with their cat in its mouth. RP's husband was able to shoot the cougar.

A dog was attacked by a cougar on RP's porch. RP pulled dog away and it has been taken to the vet. A Fish and Wildlife Officer responded with a Karelian Bear Dog. Cougar tracks were located. The search was called off due to the property line issues.

RP advised that two of their alpacas had been killed. A Fish and Wildlife Officer responded and found the cougar bedded nearby the carcasses. He took a shot at the cougar but did not locate it or any sign of a hit. A trail camera was set up.

RP advised of cougar near his home and standing in the road. RP's neighbor caught footage of a cougar in their yard. The footage was reviewed by a Fish and Wildlife Officer and confirmed to be a cougar walking through the yard.

RP was walking dog in a fenced enclosure when a cougar jumped in. RP screamed and the cougar left. When the RP went to grab her dog, a different cougar jumped into the enclosure and stared at her until she screamed, which made it leave.

Cougar jumped at a cat in the window of a house. Cougar then went nose to nose with the RP's husky, which was bigger than the cougar. A deputy responded and found the cougar in the garage. Deputy shot but did not kill cougar. Kill permit issued.
RP advised his sheep was killed and had its side torn/chewed. Advice was provided.

Goat was killed. WDFW conflict specialist and officer responded and verified a cougar was responsible. Attempts were made to track the cougar. Two sets of tracks were found but hounds lost the trail. Advice was provided.

RP noticed large cougar tracks by her porch and dog pen. RP lives in a community near the golf course. A houndsman responded and verified the cougar tracks. He used hounds to track the cougar and treed it several times. It was left unharmed.

RP came home to find his porch covered in dog hair, blood, and feces. He followed a drag mark and found the dog dead under an outbuilding. WDFW responded with a hound hunter the next day. A cougar was treed and euthanized.
Caller reported cougar sighting. Officers were unable to confirm the sighting due to a time delay.

RP shot and injured a cougar that was attacking his domestic cat. WDFW responded with a hound hunter. They followed a blood trail to a small cabin and found a cougar underneath the deck. The cougar was euthanized.
Caller had a goat killed by what she believed was a cougar. Officers attempted contact with the phone number given but were unsuccessful so it went down as unconfirmed.
RP advises that one of her sheep was killed by a cougar. She saw many large cougar tracks in the snow and has experienced cougar depredation upon her sheep over the past three years.
RP witnessed a cougar chase a deer onto her porch. The cougar tackled the deer on the porch and dragged it into the yard. WDFW responded to provide advice.
Caller reported finding tracks and a husky/malamute that had gone missing in the area. Officers were unable to confirm the sighting based off the information provided.
Caller advised of cougar problems on the property. Officers contacted the subject and issued a permit.

RP left a crawl space door open overnight and secured it shut the next day. The residents complained of something clawing under the house. RP returned and observed a very angry cougar in the crawl space, which he left open and the cougar left.
Caller reported a cougar sighting.

RP's wife witnessed a cougar attack their dog in the driveway. RP came outside and saw one cougar dragging the dog away. RP shot at the cougar. It dropped the dog and both cougars ran off. A houndsman responded and tracked and euthanized both cougars
DFW Officer received a report of a puppy being killed by a possible cougar.  The reporting party said there were two sets of tracks, one large and one small, where the attack occurred.
Caller had two cougar in her yard. Officers called and provided advice.
Caller advised her dog was taken by a cougar. Officers called conflict staff who stated this property had problems before. Biologists provided advice to the property owner and walked their property.

Two cougar kittens were treed on RP's property and an adult cougar was under a vehicle about 50 yards away. WDFW responded and advised everyone to stay inside. RP advised the kittens came out of the tree later that night and ran off with the adult.

One of RPs animals was attacked by a cougar. RP saw the cougar that night and shot it but could not find it that night. It was found the next day. WDFW responded to confirm the details of the incident.
Caller saw cougar tracks in the snow. Officers responded but could not verify what the tracks were from but appeared to be dog.
Caller reported a cougar sighting twice in one week on his property. Officers called and provided advice.
Caller had a deer killed on his property. He also saw glowing eyes while walking his dog. Officers could not determine what killed the deer so advice was given.
Caller states he saw a cougar across the lake. Officers checked the property but found no tracks in the snow.
Caller reported a cougar seen in his driveway. Officers reported the sighting as it ran when he had gone to check his traps nearby.
Caller reported a cougar that came up to get her cat. Officers called and provided advice.
Caller was walking his dog when a cougar hissed at them. Officers provided advice as an animal was not seen.
Caller reported a deer kill in his orchard by a cougar The cougar was seen but no depredations confirmed. Advice was given.

Caller had alpacas killed by a cougar. Officers responded to move the cougar trap and confirmed it was killed by one. Officers set the trap on his property. It was checked on 1/17 and had no activity.

Contacted by landowner stating he lost 5 cattle in 1 1/2 weeks.  Two dead calves and 1 dead adult cow still on property. Necropsies performed on all three animals.  The two calves were confirmed  cougar kill.  Cause of death for adult cow is unknown.
RP's llama was killed and dragged approximately 30 yards to a fence through which the predator could not get the llama out. WDFW responded and verified that cougar was responsible.

RP had a buck goat killed, said there were huge tracks around the carcass. WDFW responded and verified that a cougar was responsible. Karelian Bear Dog was deployed but the search was called off due to property boundary issues.
RP's wife saw a cougar trying to get their dog through the fence. A WDFW officer called to provide advice.
Caller advised there was a dead deer on her property killed by a cougar. Officers provided advice.

RPs dog went missing and he found blood, fur, drag marks, and tracks outside. A WDFW officer responded, located the dog carcass, and verified it was a cougar kill. The officer found an emaciated male cougar nearby and dispatched it.
Caller found cougar tracks around her residence. Officers called and were K9 not cougar.
Caller advised of a cougar sighting. Officers provided information.

RP witnessed a cougar eating a deer in the woodshed. A WDFW Officer responded and verified the presence of cougar and deer tracks in the area. No action was taken to track or euthanize the cougar since it did not display dangerous behavior.
Caller reported a cougar walking down the roadway. Officers provided her information.

Caller reported cougar sighting near his home. Officers and hounds responded. They found cougar tracks. Officers were told that the wife had ended up trying to scare off the cougar with warning shots and may have hit it. Due to the injury they pulled the hounds- the cougar also got into an area that was unsafe to pursue on foot.
Caller reported a cougar frequenting her property. Officers provided advice as the cougar had done nothing to cause alarm.
Caller advised of a cougar at her residence.Officers provided advice and notified conflict staff.
Caller reported a cougar killed three goats Saturday. Officers responded and were unable to confirm as the carcasses had been buried by the owner and the other carcass not located.
Caller advised there was a cougar sighting. Officers ran K9s and deployed traps but had no hits on either.
Caller saw a cougar walking on their porch. Officer responded and found K9 tracks not cougar.
Caller had a cougar in her backyard. Officers responded and did not strike on any cougar tracks.
Caller had a sheep killed by a cougar. Officers responded and verified it was actually done by coyotes.
Caller lost a sheep to what they thought was a cougar. Officers responded and confirmed it was killed by coyotes.
Caller called regarding the cougar on Vashon Island. She just wanted an update and hadn't seen the cougar.
RP advised that his domestic cat had been killed and there were cougar tracks at the scene. He has had several cougar depredations in the past. WDFW gave advice.

RP let his dog out and it did not return as usual. He went outside and found that his dog had been killed and there were cougar tracks and drag marks around. A houndsman responded and his hounds located the cougar which was euthanized.

A cougar came after RP's dog while he was letting it out. Dog not injured. RP fired his handgun which did not seem to scare the cougar. RP has video of the cougar and her four kittens on his property. WDFW K9 unit responded, no cougar located.

RP found his dog deceased under the porch in the morning. RP witnessed a cougar run out from under the porch. That night, the cougar was back under the porch. RP shot and killed the cougar when it came out.
Caller thought a cougar was on his property stalking his horses. He only saw the eyes at night. Officers provided information.

RP heard his two dogs barking and went outside and saw a cougar sitting uphill of one his sheep, which was dead. He shot at and hit the cougar and it ran off. WDFW officers responded and hounds were deployed. They located and dispatched the cougar.

RP found his boxer dog dead in the morning and saw a cougar run out from under the porch. The cougar was under the porch again later that evening and the RP shot and killed the cougar. WDFW responded to collect the cougar carcass.

RP had a goat killed. WDFW Officers responded with a hound hunter and confirmed the presence of cougar tracks, drag marks, and saw a cougar walking away from a brushy area where the goat carcass was cached and fed upon. The cougar was euthanized.
Caller found cougar tracks near her barn. Officers provided advice as she wasn't concerned.
Cougar hanging around neighborhood for past month. RP has lost two domestic cats, presumably to cougar. RP's neighbor has a picture of the cougar on his porch. WDFW called to provide advice.
Caller found fresh cougar tracks. Officers provided advice.
RP wanted to report cougar sighting in his area.  He said it has been sighted a few times.  Is not aggressive or depredating on livestock or otherwise causing public safety concern
Caller reported a cougar near the Colville Jr High. Officers called and responded with K9 to the location. They located no signs of a cougar.
Caller believed a cougar killed a moose near his property. Officers responded and were unable to cross the river to access the carcass.
Caller advised of a cougar sighting in the area over the last few months. Officers called and provided advice.
Cougar chasing RPs domestic cats on his porch. WDFW provided advice.
Caller caught a cougar and four kittens on her game camera. Officers responded to the address and confirmed the sighting.
Caller advised of many cougar sightings near their residence. Officers emailed back advice.
CALLER A COUGAR HANGING AROUND HIS NEIGHBORHOOD FOR THE LAST MONTH.  HE HAS LOST TWO CATS, HE ASSUMES TO THE COUGAR. OFFICERS PROVIDED INFO.

Cougar seen multiple times walking through town, through a garage, and on trails where children and others are walking. It does not seem to be afraid of humans. WDFW called and advised to call if the cougar is seen during daylight hours.
Caller advised of multiple cougar sightings near her home. Officers called and provided advice.
Caller advised of a cougar hanging around their property. Officers responded with advice.
Caller had a deer killed near his horses. Due to multiple sightings in the area permits were issued.

Caller  advised there was a cougar on his property. Officers called but weren't able to get much information from the person who answered the phone. The original caller called back later and provided more information. It was unconfirmed.
Caller reported a cougar that passed through their yard. Officers provided advice.
Caller reported injured deer in their yard that they thought was attacked by a cougar. Officers could not confirm
Caller advised they had cougar tracks on their property. Officers called and provided advice.
Caller reported a cougar sighting while walking her dog. Officers provided information.
Citizen found cougar tracks in the snow. He sent in pictures. Officers provided advice.

RP observed what appeared to be a cougar running away as she pulled into the driveway. RP found one of her pygmy goats dead. WDFW responded and verified that the wounds and eating patterns were consistent with a cougar. Advice given.
Caller had a cougar on his property. Advice was given.
Caller found cougar tracks in their neighborhood. Officers provided advice.
Caller reported finding cougar scat at his rental cabin. Officers could not confirm.
Caller found possible cougar tracks. Officers called for more information and to get images. Officers confirmed it was either a bobcat or small cougar.
Caller saw a cougar near her residence. Deputies had checked the area and found no record. Officers responded as well but found no tracks.
Caller was missing a calf. Officers provided advice was the cougar was not seen and the calf was not found.
Caller had a cougar sitting on their deck. Images confirmed it was a cougar.
Caller had a dead deer under his cabin. He thought it was related to a cougar. It was unconfirmed.
Caller stated she saw two cougars near her home. Advice was given.
Caller reported a cougar under their deck. Officers took the report as sighting because it had not done anything aggressive.
Caller found a deceased cougar near his residence. Officers collected the cougar to perform a necropsy.
Caller advised of a cougar in his field. Officers called and provided advice as the caller had livestock.
Caller advised one of their goats was killed. Officers responded and found no evidence of depredation. They were unable to confirm.
Caller advised an animal damaged his jeep. Officers called and provided him advice as there were no tracks.
RP found five dead goats in the pen. DFW responded and called out a hound hunter. The cougar was located and euthanized.
Dead cougar was found on the C hill above Cashmere by Nahaum Canyon. May have died from natural causes. No evidence of being shot.
Caller had a cougar in his tree. Officers offered to come haze it but the caller declined and would rather have the cougar leave on it's own.
Caller advised a cougar was in their backyard. Officers responded and found no presence of a cougar but did find raccoons.

RP witnessed their domestic dog being taken by a cougar. RP shot at the cougar, unsure if it was hit. WDFW Officers responded with a Karelian Bear Dog and located the deceased dog, cougar tracks, and a cougar blood trail. Unable to locate cougar.
Caller advised a cougar crossed the roadway. Officers provided advice.
Caller advised he saw a cougar. Officers called and provided advice and were informed they had only seen tracks. Officers confirmed they were not cougar tracks.
Caller saw a cougar cross through her property and go down an embankment. Officers provided information.
Caller had two cougars on her porch. Officers asked for images and confirmed it was cougars.
Caller advised of a cougar sighting on his property. Officers had been to the residence before for depredations. They set a new trap.

RP advised two of his goats had disappeared. WDFW responded with a Karelian Bear Dog. They were unable to find the carcasses but a cougar was treed, immobilized, and processed by a WDFW biologist for an ongoing study.

RP was walking his daughter to the bus stop when he saw a cougar. It ran away when he yelled. RP also advises he had cougars in his front yard two days prior. It is probable that RP sighted a female who has been seen in the area with three kittens.
RP advised that a cougar killed a deer in her backyard. The deer was partially eaten and dragged under a tree. This occurred in a densely forested area on the southeast side of Nahwatzel Lake.
Caller advised a cougar had been seen in the area on a few occasions. Officers provided advice as the caller had not seen it.
CALLER SAW A COUGAR ON HER FRONT PORCH, RAN OFF TO THE SOUTH.  THINKS IT MAY HAVE BEEN IN HER BARN EARLIER THAT EVENING. OFFICERS CALLED AND PROVIDED ADVICE.
Caller found cougar tracks. Officers were unable to confirm and provided advice.
Caller saw a cougar at the country club. Officers provided advice.
Caller saw a cougar on her property. Officers provided advice.

Caller advised of a cougar sighting near a small barn. Officers and deputies responded unable to find the cougar. They located tracks that fit a cougar in size. Hounds were called out but were unsuccessful.
Caller saw a cougar run in to a barn. Officers responded and couldn't locate it. They called out hounds who were unable to locate a cougar.

RP let his dog out and it went toward an elk carcass nearby and he was unable to call the dog back. A neighbor found evidence of a dog/cougar fight near the elk. The dog was taken to the vet and died. The cougar is being hunted.
RP has seen cougars on her trail camera for the pas three days. RP has video of the cougar chasing deer. No safety concerns. The cougar has not attacked her horses or dogs.
Caller reported cougar in his barn. Officers and conflict staff responded. Officers provided advice as the carcass found in their barn appeared old and cause of death was not confirmed.
Caller had a cougar kill a deer next to their house. Officers removed the deer and provided advice.
Caller reported a cougar in her yard. Officers called and got pictures of the tracks left but were unable to confirm it was a cougar.

RP went to feed chickens and found a cougar near the coop. She also believes the cougar may have tried to attack her miniature pony. A Deputy responded and the cougar was still in the yard, hissing and growling at him. The Deputy shot the cougar.
Caller reported a cougar sighting. He did not request contact.
Caller found a deer killed by what they thought was a cougar. Officers called and provided information on living with wildlife.

RP's animals have been on edge the last few weeks. There have been cougar tracks in the snow around the barn and her yard. Neighbors have also seen the cougar. RP has history of cougar depredation on property.
Caller saw a cougar two weeks prior and likely had tracks on their property in the snow. Officers called and provided advice.

RP who has had cougar depredations in the past came home to see a cougar in his driveway. The cougar ran toward the barn and livestock. A houndsman responded and pursued the cougar away from the property. The cougar was not harmed.
RP was missing one head of cattle and found the carcass. WDFW responded with a hound hunter and located and euthanized a large male cougar.
Caller had a dead deer in his driveway that he thought was killed by a cougar. Officers called and stated it likely was a cougar kill but provided advice.
Caller had heard of a cougar in the area and had found tracks. Officers responded and were unable to locate any tracks.
Caller had two cougar sightings- One on the 9th and one on the 10th. Officers called and provided advice and responded to the area. No tracks found. 68th and Inglewood.
Caller reported cougar tracks in their front yard. Officers called but the cougar tracks were gone.
Caller reported a cougar sighting crossing the roadway. Unconfirmed.
Caller saw a cougar cross through the owners porch.
A dead cougar kitten was found in a batting cage net at Hofstetter Elementary School. No signs of foul play.
Caller caught a cougar on her camera walking through the property on 2/25.
Caller advised security had received report of a cougar sighting. Officers provided advice.

RP saw a cougar on the hill behind his residence. Cougar was about 100 yards away and about 70-80 pounds. He last observed the cougar walking southbound through the grass. Cougar was not causing any problems.
Caller had a cougar in her driveway. Officers provided advice as they could not locate tracks to confirm.
Caller had a sheep killed in his pasture. Officers responded and found a dead ram. It was confirmed by officers and biologist to be a coyote kill based on evidence.
Caller saw cougar tracks near the church. Officers could not find cougar tracks but did find domestic dog tracks.
Caller advised a cougar or a tiger was on their roof. Officers responded and could find no evidence of a cougar or tiger being in the area.
Caller advised he saw a cougar on the neighbor's property. Officers called and provided advice.
Caller advised they heard something walking on their roof. Officers called and responded to the area. They checked tracks that all appeared to be K9. Officers provided advice.

DFW Officers received a report of a cougar that had been sighted in the reporting party's backyard over the last three nights.  She was advised to keep her pets inside and call immediately if seen again.
Caller had a deer killed on his property. Officers investigated and found that the deer was not killed by a cougar.
RECEIVED  A CALL REPORTING THREE GOATS KILLED BY TWO COUGARS.  OFFICERS REPSONDED WITH HOUND HANDLERS AND DISPATCHED THREE COUGARS OVER THE COURSE OF TWO DAYS.
Caller reported a cougar sighting. Officers documented it.

Caller had five alpacas killed on 3/28/2017. Officers forwarded pictures taken to the cougar specialist at DFW who confirmed it was likely a young cougar responsible. Officers told the property owner if it returned it could be lethally removed.
Caller advised of a cougar was on her back porch. Officers called and left advice via voicemail.
Caller had two lambs go missing that were less than a week old. They suspected a cougar was responsible based on tracks found. Officers called and provided advice.
RP ADVISED HE FOUND COUGAR TRACKS ON FRONT PORCH AND SENT PHOTOS TO WDFW.  OFFICER CONFIRMED THE TRACKS WERE MOST LIKELY COUGAR TRACKS.  ADVICE PROVIDED.
Caller advised her persian cat was taken by a cougar. Officers called and provided advice.
Caller advised several sheep had been killed or injured. Officers responded and based on evidence determined it to be domestic dogs.

DFW Officers received a report of a deer that the homeowner believed was killed by a cougar.  Officers viewed the carcass and confirmed the injuries were consistent with a cougar.  Officers advised the homeowner on actions to take regarding the cat.
Caller stated she saw a cougar running through a wooded area while on a walk. Officers called and provided advice.
Caller advised there have been multiple sightings on the island. RP had sent in images that were inconclusive of cougar tracks.
Caller advised she thinks a cougar scared her goats. Officers responded and provided advice after finding out it wasn't a cougar took her goat.
Called stating he found a fresh cougar kill in his meadows. Officers responded to do a necropsy and confirmed it was not a cougar kill.

LANDOWNERS WERE ALERTED TO A COUGAR ON THEIR PROPERTY BY NEIGHBORS.  THAT EVENING THEY FOUND A DEAD CALF THAT HAD BEEN DRUG UNDER A FENCE.  WOUNDS THAT WERE CONSISTENT WITH A COUGAR WERE NOTED ON THE CALF CARCASS.  A PERMIT WAS ISSUED.
Callers stated cougars had been in the area the last few days and a goat had been killed. Officers responded but confirmed a cougar was not the responsible party for the goat's death.
COUGAR WAS SEEN LAYING IN BACK YARD NOT BOTHERING ANYTHING.  REPORTING PARTY WAS ABLE TO TAKE A PHOTO OF THE COUGAR WHICH WAS CONFIRMED BY A DFW OFFICER AS BEING A COUGAR.

DFW Officer received a report of a cougar looking through a window in the reporting party's home.  The tracks left by the animal were described as being consistent with cougar tracks.  He was advised to view the Living with Wildlife webpage.
Caller advised that a cougar has been seen in the neighborhood. It had also killed a deer. Officers responded and were unable to verify the cause of death on the deer.
Caller had free range chickens killed by what she thought was a cougar. Officers called and provided advice to secure her livestock.
Caller had a deer killed in his yard by a suspected cougar. Officers could not verify whether or not a cougar killed it based on evidence left. Officers provided advice.
Cougar sighted on front deck-- marked the deck.

CALF WAS REPORTED KILLED BY A POSS COUGAR.  OFFICER RESPONDED AND IT APPEARED THE CALF WAS NOT KILLED BY A CANINE ANIMAL DUE TO THE CONDITION OF THE CALF.  ATTEMPTS TO LOCATE A COUGAR WERE UNSUCCESSFUL.
Caller advised a cougar came onto her porch. Officers called and provided advice.
Officers received numerous reports of a cougar in Wilkeson. Officers placed game cameras on the properties to catch images of it but were unsuccessful.
Caller had a newborn calf killed by a cougar. Report shows an unconfirmed.

A COUGAR WAS SEEN LAYING IN THE GRASS NOT BEING AGGRESSIVE.  A LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER ON SCENE OBSERVED THE COUGAR WALK INTO THE WOODS.  A CHECK OF THE AREA CONFIRMED NUMEROUS DEER TRACKS AND WOODED AREA.  ADVICE WAS GIVEN TO THE REPORTING PARTY.
Caller advised of an unknown predator that attacked their horse. Officers looked at images provided and explained that this was likely due to coyotes.
COUGAR WAS SPOTTED.
Anonymous caller left a VM stating they saw a cougar while walking on the trails at Medical Lake.
Caller advised of a cougar sighting while walking. Officers provided advice.

A GOAT WAS REPORTED KILLED AND DRUG ACROSS A PASTURE.  OFFICERS RESPONDED AND FOUND ONE SMALL PUNCTURE WOUND TO THE NECK AND PLACED GAME CAMERAS OBSERVING THE CARCASS.  A COUGAR WAS SEEN DURING THE NIGHT AND OFFICIALS WERE ABLE TO TRACK THE COUGAR.
Caller reported a cougar sighting in the area. Regional office staff provided advice.
Caller advised her homeless friend had to punch a cougar in the nose that was chasing her.. Officers called and provided advice. This was unconfirmed.
Caller captured a cougar on their camera. It was not doing anything wrong so the sighting was documented.
Caller saw a cougar on the hillside. Officers provided information.
Caller stated his son saw a cougar. Advice was given.
Caller saw a cougar while walking her dog. Advice was given

COUGAR WAS SPOTTED IN A TREE NEAR PETS, LIVESTOCK AND CHILDREN.  DFW OFFICERS INVESTIGATED AND DETERMINED THE LANDOWNER WAS JUSTIFIED IN DISPATCHING THE COUGAR  DUE TO THE PROXIMITY THE COUGAR WAS IN RELATION TO HUMANS AND DOMESTIC ANIMALS.
Caller reported a cougar sighting. No call back was requested.
COUGAR WAS SEEN IN A STARE DOWN WITH LANDOWNERS DOG.  THE COUPLE BEGAN YELLING AT THE COUGAR AND IT RAN AWAY.  REPORTING PARTY COULD NOT DETERMINE IF IT WAS AN ADULT OR JUVENILE COUGAR.
Caller had a cougar returning to their property. Officers called and provided advice.

REPORTING PARTY REPORTED BEING STALKED BY A COUGAR.  HE BELIEVED THE COUGAR MAY HAVE CUBS NEARBY.  DFW OFFICER AND KARELIAN BEAR DOG ATTEMPTED TO LOCATE COUGAR.  THEY FOUND EVIDENCE OF FEEDING DEER AND ADVICE WAS PROVIDED ON FEEDING WILDLIFE.
Caller saw a cougar in his backyard. Officers called and provided advice.
REPORTING PARTY STATED HE WITNESSED A COUGAR KILL AND DRAG AWAY AN ALPACA.  HE SAID HE BURIED THE CARCASS AND THE COUGAR RETURNED AND DUG IT UP AGAIN.
Caller had a sheep attacked by a cougar. Officers had biologist do a site visit and confirmed it likely was due to cougar.
ALPACA WAS TAKEN BY A COUGAR SOMETIME BETWEEN SATURDAY NIGHT AND SUNDAY MORNING.  THE ALPACA WAS PULLED OVER A FENCE AND DRUG INTO THE WOODLINE.
LAMB WAS FOUND DEAD IN PASTURE WITH ONE BITE WOUND TO THE NECK.  NO TRACKS COULD BE FOUND.  CAMERAS WERE SET UP OVER CARCASS WITH NO ACTIVITY CAPTURED BY CAMERAS.
DFW Officers received a report of a landowner reporting a young cougar spotted 5 June 2017 in a tree overlooking a cattle drinking hole. Property owner lost one calf in March, possibly to predation.

CALF WAS KILLED AND DRUG INTO THE WOODS AND PARTIALLY COVERED.  CAMERAS WERE SET UP AND CAPTURED PHOTOS OF A COUGAR FEEDING ON THE CALF CARCASS.  A TRAP WAS SET UP WITH CAMERAS AND NO FURTHER ACTIVITY WAS IDENTIFIED.

DFW Officers received a report of a cougar that was seen by a landowner.  The man fired a warning shot in the direction of the cougar and the cougar ran off.  Officers answered the questions regarding his rights to defend his family.
Caller advised he heard what he thought was a cougar. There was no way to confirm. Advice was given.
Caller had a calf killed by a cougar. He had prints that he thought were cougar. He set up a trail camera. He was provided advice.
Caller reported two goats found killed. Officers responded and could not verify the culprit.

Caller saw a cougar in his neighborhood and it jumped a 6' fence.  Staff directed him to the “Living with Wildlife Cougar” information and told him I would pass along his information to enforcement and biologist.  No call expected.
Caller saw a cougar walking behind their property. Advice was given.
Caller stated her husband saw a cougar headed towards a neighborhood. Officers responded with hounds and found no scent of a cougar.
Caller reported a cougar in her yard. Officers were unable to confirm as no picture was retrieved.

HIKER SAW A COUGAR WATCHING THEM ON THE CENTENNIAL TRAIL APPROXIMATELY ONE QUARTER MILE SOUTH OF WHERE THE TRAIL ENDS AND THE ROAD BEGINS.  HIKER USED BINOCULARS TO OBSERVE THE COUGAR BEFORE IT WALKED AWAY.
OWNER OF A DECEASED COW TOOK AN OFFICER TO THE SITE OF THE CARCASS.  UPON EXAMINATION OF THE CARCASS IT WAS PROBABLE THAT A COUGAR WAS RESPONSIBLE FOR THE DEPREDATION.

DFW Officers were notified of two calves being taken by a cougar over the last two weeks.  The carcasses had already been buried before the Officers arrived.  Landowners were advised to leave any more carcasses in place if it happens in the future.

RESIDENT WAS WORKING OUTSIDE AND ENTERED THEIR RESIDENCE FOR A COFFEE.  THE PERSON NOTICED A COUGAR WALK BY OUTSIDE NEAR THE DOOR THEY HAD JUST ENTERED.  THE COUGAR HAS NOT BEEN SEEN SINCE.  A SALT LICK TO ATTRACT DEER WAS RECOMMEDED TO BE REMOVED.
DFW Officers received report of a cougar that was below a homeowners deck looking up at him and his dog.  Homeowners neighbor called as he was concerned for his livestock.
Caller advised one of his ponies was attacked by a cougar. Officers and conflict staff stated the wounds were consistent with that of a cougar but don't confirm that it was one.
Caller saw a cougar while walking her dog. Officers provided advice.
Caller had a sheep eaten on their property. Officers responded with dogs and conflict staff. It ended up being coyote kill.

RESIDENT REPORTED SEEING A COUGAR SITTING ADJACENT TO HIS YARD IN THE BRUSH NEAR HIS WOOD PILE.  DFW OFFICER REPSONDED BUT THE COUGAR HAD LEFT THE AREA BEFORE OFFICER ARRIVED.  OFFICER SEARCHED THE AREA AND FOUND OLD SCRATCH MARKS ON  A TREE.
LIVESTOCK WAS DEPREDATED BY A COUGAR.  DFW OFFICERS AUTHORIZED USED OF PURSUIT HOUNDS TO TRACK COUGAR.
Caller was reporting she saw a cougar cross Selah Naches Road, near Old Stage Way. Officers contacted the citizen who stated it ran towards an adjacent field. Officers provided advice.

A COUGAR WAS SHOOT AND KILLED AT A RESIDENCE WHERE ONE OR TWO DAYS PRIOR THE RESIDENT HAD LOST A CAT.  WHEN HE SAW THE COUGAR IN HIS YARD HE THOUGHT IT WAS GOING AFTER HIS OTHER PETS.  SAMPLES WERE TAKEN AND THE HEAD WAS SAVED FOR EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE
CALLER ADVISED HER NEIGHBOR SIGHTING OF THE COUGAR THIS MORNING.  OFFICERS CALLED AND PROVIDED ADVICE. SHE HAD NOT SEEN THE CAT HERSELF.
Caller reported a cougar on their property. Officers called and arrived on scene to track cougar. Dogs were unable to locate it.

RESIDENT SPOTTED A COUGAR ON THEIR FRONT PORCH AT 0555.  THE COUGAR LEFT THE AREA AND THE RESIDENT WAS ABLE TO GET TWO PHOTOS.  DFW OFFICER CONFIRMED THE PHOTOS WERE OF A COUGAR.  THE COUGAR WAS NOT ABLE TO BE LOCATED.
Caller reported seeing a cougar under the powerlines.
Caller advised of cougar prints found on her property. Officers responded and set up cameras but captured no footage.
Caller saw one female cougar and three cubs. Officers responded and saw three coyotes in the area observed.
Caller lost a goat to what they thought was a cougar. Officers responded and set up a camera.
COUGAR WAS SEEN WALKING ACROSS STREET IN REPUBLIC.  SIGHTING WAS FIRST REPORTED TO FERRY COUNTY SHERIFF.
Caller advised a cougar was in her tree. Officers searched with hounds but had no success.
Caller reported a cougar crossed the road in front of his vehicle. Officers responded with hounds and found no scent.

RESIDENT REPORTED FINDING A DEAD EWE AND TWO LAMBS MISSING.  DFW OFFICER RESPONDED AND AFTER VIEWING THE CARCASS CONFIRMED THE WOUNDS WERE CONSISTENT WITH A COUGAR.  SEARCH OF THE AREA BY DFW RESOURCES DID NOT RESULT IN LOCATING A COUGAR.
REPORTING PARTY SAW A COUGAR CROSS THE ROAD IN HER NEIGHBORHOOD.  DFW OFFICER PROVIDED ADVICE ON COUGAR BEHAVIOR AND ASKED RP TO PASS THE INFORMATION ON TO HER NEIGHBORS.
Caller saw a cougar on the property. Officers responded and could not verify or find any tracks belonging to a cougar. Advice was provided.
Caller stated her husband saw a cougar on the island a week prior. Officers attempted to call the citizen back and provide updates on trapping the cougar.
Caller advised there was a cougar sighting which was a third hand report. Unconfirmed.
Caller had a cougar on her back deck. Officers were unable to get back in contact with the caller for verification.
Caller advised of a cougar frequenting the property. Officers called and provided advice and believed the animal to actually be a bobcat.
REPORTING PARTY CONTACTED WASHINGTON STATE PATROL REPORTING A COUGAR KILLED LIVESTOCK.  THEY REPORTED TWO GOATS AND A LAMB WERE KILLED BY A COUGAR.  DFW OFFICER CONFIRMED THE REPORT.

RP WAS WALKING BACK DOWN FROM FIXING A FENCE WHEN SHE SAW A COUGAR 10 FEET AWAY FROM HER.  THE COUGAR DID NOT ACT AGGRESSIVELY TOWARD HER AND WAS NOT AFRAID OF HER DOG.  A HOUNDSMAN WAS AUTHORIZED TO CHASE THE COUGAR AWAY.
Caller saw a cougar in her pasture. Officers called and provided advice.
REPORTING PARTY CAME HOME FROM VACATION AND FOUND TWO NUBIAN GOATS HAD BEEN KILLED.  ONE WAS HALF EATEN AND THE OTHER WAS DRUG OVER A FENCE.
Caller reported a cougar took his two domestic cats. Officers called and provided advice and were advised they hadn't seen cougars since the cats were taken.
Caller found a deceased fawn that had been scavenged on. Officers could not confirm it was a cougar but they are know to be in the area.
REPORTING PARTY CONTACTED WDF TO REPORT A COUGAR THAT WAS WALKING ALONG A BLUFF NEAR A COFFEE SHOP IN ZILLAH.  THE COUGAR WAS NOT ACTING AGGRESSIVE AND JUST LEISURELY WALKING ALONG THE YAKIMA RIVER.

RP report possible cougar depredation on calf.  Carcass was disposed of prior to WDFW arrival.  Only predator sign in area was coyote scat.  RP advised to leave carcass as it lay and contact us if occurs again.

Caller thought she had a cougar laying in her barn. Officers spoke with neighbors who stated there were many stray dogs in the area that fit the description given. Officers responded to the area and were unable to find evidence of a cougar.
Caller advised a goat was killed by a cougar. Officers responded with conflict staff and a local houndsman. After a necropsy it was determined that the likely predator was a dog.

REPORTING PARTY CONTACTED DFW REPORTING SIX DEAD SHEEP AND ONE LAMB MISSING.  DFW OFFICER RESPONDED AND CONTACTED A HOUNDSMAN TO ASSIST.  ONE PORTION OF THE FENCE WAS BENT OVER AND THAT WAS DETERMINED THE POINT OF ENTRY FOR THE COUGAR.
REPORTING PARTY CONTACTED DFW REPORTING A LARGE COUGAR NEXT TO HIS HOUSE.  DFW OFFICER CONTACTED RP AND DISCUSSED THE INCIDENT AND WHAT PRECAUTIONS TO TAKE.
Caller reported a deer killed by a cougar. Officers made contact and could not find confirmation of a cougar.
Caller's neighbor saw a cougar sunbathing. Officers called and provided advice.
WDFW Officer received a report of a cougar.

RECEIVED A REPORT OF A COUGAR IN THE MIDDLE OF THE ROAD.  REPORTING PARTY SAW THE COUGAR HEAD TOWARD A NEIGHBOR'S AND TOOK A PHOTO.  DFW OFFICER RESPONDED AND MET WITH THE RP WHO SHOWED THE PHOTO.  DFW OFFICER CONFIRMED IT WAS A COUGAR.
RECEIVED A REPORT OF A POSSIBLE LIVESTOCK DEPREDATION BY A COUGAR.  REPORTING PARTY STATED A COUGAR KILLED A GOAT DURING THE NIGHT.  DFW OFFICER RESPONDED AND CONFIRMED THE COUGER DEPREDATION REPORT.
Caller advised one of the foals had an injury to it's leg and back. Officers confirmed the marks weren't consistent with a cougar.
Caller had a cougar in their front yard. They did not request a call back from an officer.

RECEIVED A REPORT OF A COUGAR COMING ON THE PROPERTY.  DFW OFFICER CONTACTED RP AND ADVISED HER ON TRYING TO DISCOURAGE THE COUGAR BY USING A RADIO, LIGHTS, AND TRYING TO SCARE OFF DEER.  ALSO PROVIDED ADVICE ON HER RIGHT TO PROTECT HERSELF.
Caller reported a cougar frequenting their property. Officers called but got no answer.
Caller advised there was one deceased and one injured goat on the property. Officers responded with conflict staff. Based on investigation it was determined that the cause of death was unknown.
Caller advised of a possible cougar sighting. Officers responded to the school in the area to provided advice and check the property. They found no sign of a cougar.

DFW Officers received a report of a cougar that was shot by a homeowner while it was inside a sheep pen.  The cat had killed seven sheep.  DFW Officers confirmed the situation and a camera was used over the carcasses to ensure no other cat returned.

Caller lost four to five calves to an unknown predator. He was unable to find any of the carcasses or evidence on how they were killed. Officers contacted conflict staff and had them contact the citizen.
Caller advised a cougar had been seen in the area. He found scratch marks on a power pole that he thought were from the cat. Officers were unable to confirm.

Caller had an alpaca killed by what they believed was a cougar. Officers responded and could not determine the cause of death but set a cougar trap. Nothing was captured so it was removed three days later.
Caller reported a sheep attacked by what he thought was a cougar. Officers were unable to contact him back and follow up.

Caller reported two cougars that were seen running away from a deceased calf on his property. Officers called and were told the cattle had broken down fencing. When he went out he found the dead calf. It was raining to heavily for hounds to come out the same day so they responded the next morning. The hounds were unsuccessful.
Caller had a sheep killed in his pasture. Officers responded and confirmed it likely was a cougar and a trap was set.

Caller had a ram killed by a cougar. Officers responded and performed a necropsy where it was determined that it likely was NOT a cougar kill. Officers contacted a hound hunt for the property owner as she was certain a cougar lived in the area but he was unable to locate a sign of cougar.

DFW Officers received a report of children on bicycles seeing a cougar in the area.  DFW Officers responded and were unable to locate a cougar.  One citizen had photos of a cougar and they were provided to the officers.
Caller reported he and a friend heard a cougar screaming while on the golf course. Officers called and provided advice.
Cougar ran across the callers property. Officers provided advice.
Caller advised a cougar came through the yard. Officers called because she requested they be trapped. They provided advice.
Caller reported a cougar sighting. Officers provided advice but found no evidence to confirm.
Caller reported a cougar sighting. They were contacted and provided advice.
Caller reported two cougars on her property. Officers were unable to reach the original reporting party so this was unconfirmed.

RP contacted DFW office and during the conversation reported there had been a cougar spotted in a field behind her residence.  RP stated the cougar was not bothering anyone.  A DFW Officer provided advice and to call and report the cougar if seen.

RP contacted DFW to report a cougar had come up on her porch and laid down for ten minutes.  The cougar left when a deer walked by.  RP was able to take a photo of the cat which an officer confirmed was a cougar, estimated to be less than two years.

RP contacted region office to report three sheep were killed overnight.  DFW Officer viewed the carcasses and determined they had signs consistent with a cougar depredation.  Area was checked with no sign of a cougar.
CALLER ADVISED OF A COUGAR SEEN IN THE AREA. CALLER HAD NOT SEEN IT HERSELF.

DFW Officer was contacted regarding the previous night a cougar startled a resident when she returned home.  The cougar ran off when she screamed.  Her husband chased the cat off through a field.  They were explained their rights to defend themselves

DFW Officers received a call of a possible attack by a cougar on a dog.  During the night the dog's owner heard noise outside and let their dog back in.  Later the dog was observed with a cut and some puncture wounds.  The cat was not located.
CALLER REPORTED COUGAR SIGHTING IN THE APPLE ORCHARD ACROSS FROM HER RESIDENCE. OFFICERS PROVIDED ADVICE.

DFW Officer was contacted with a report of a cougar in a tree the previous night.  The resident's dogs treed a cougar, she fired one warning shot into the air to scare off the cougar and it jumped out of the tree and ran off.
Caller reported two cougars sitting in his driveway.
CALLER STATED THAT A COUGAR JUST WALKED ACROSS HER PROPERTY. UNCONFIRMED.
CALLER ADVISED COUGARS IN HIS DRIVEWAY. OFFICERS CALLED AND PROVIDED ADVICE.
Caller advised that their domestic cat was killed. Officers reviewed pictures but could not confirm what was responsible. Officers provided advice.
Caller advised of a cougar crossing through their yard. Officers provided advice.
Observed cougar attempting to get into neighbors chicken coup.  Cougar was unsuccessful.  Advised.
RP reported seeing a cougar walk out of their neighbors yard at 3 am.  There were additional reports that confirmed the sighting of a cougar in the area.
Caller advised they heard cougars screaming. They also thought they found scat. WILDCOMM provided advice.
Caller had a chicken killed. A cougar was seen in the coop. Officers provided advice.
Caller witnessed a cougar jump on on her kitten outside. Officers responded to the area but they couldn't locate any evidence to confirm that it was a cougar.
Reporting party reported two cougars that were bedded down in his back yard.  RP said there had been other sightings in the area and wanted to report the sighting.
Caller reported two cougars in their yard. Unconfirmed
Caller heard a cougar on her back porch. Officers called and provided advice.
Caller saw a cougar cross the roadway. Officers called and provided advice.
Caller reported a cougar on the campground. Officers called for more information and provided advice. Officers checked the campground and found no evidence of cougar.
RP heard a noise and then saw a cougar walking across pasture coming from the area where the noise was.  The cougar was last seen walking toward a river.  The RP was not concerned about the cat.
Cougar was observed walking down a street into a cul de sac.  The cougar was not reported as causing any issues and was not able to be located.

DFW Officer received a report of a sheep being taken by a possible cougar.  Officer arrived and confirmed the dead sheep had claw marks and bite marks consistent with a cougar.  Hounds man was unable to locate the cougar.
Caller advised that she heard a cougar outside her residence. Officers tried calling her for more information but were unable to reach her.

Two reports of a cougar that walked from the neighborhood into an orchard.  DFW Officer responded and could not locate the cougar.  The cougar was not causing any issues and walked into an area with many orchards.

Reporting party saw a cougar run in front of her car while driving home.  The cougar ran through some yards before RP lost sight of the cougar.  RP saw the picture of a cougar on Facebook and recognized the animal.
Caller reported a cougar on their deck. It was described as skinny and when he clapped the animal sauntered off. Officers called and provided advice.
Caller reported a cougar in the orchard behind his home. Officers tried to follow up but the number provided was invalid.
Callers advised that domestic cats had been doing missing. All thought it was due to a cougar seen in the area. Officers monitored the reports but were unable to confirm the sightings.
Teacher from Montessori school called to report a large paw print found on top of a sandbox.  DFW Officer observed the print and provided information to the school on cougars.

DFW Officer and Conflict Specialist responded to a report of a calf being killed by a possible cougar.  The carcass was a couple days old and had been eaten on by birds.  After a thorough investigation it was determined a cougar had killed the calf.

Cougar was spotted in a backyard at night while two people were sitting outside after grilling.  The people were able to safely get inside and did not see where the cougar went to.  Officers and dogs were used but could not locate a cougar.
Caller had two sheep killed. Officers responded and verified that the sheep had been killed by dogs or coyotes.
Caller advised a miniature horse had been attacked by a cougar. Officers were unable to confirm as the wounds were not consistent with a cougar attack.
Caller had a goat killed on his property. Officers set up a trail camera as the caller had disposed of the carcass. Officers were unable to confirm.

DFW Officer received a report with photos of a cougar that was on the deck of the reporting party the previous night.  DFW Officer provided advice on future sightings with the importance of timely reporting.
Caller advised of a cougar sighting on their property. Officers responded and found dog tracks in the area where the cougar was seen. Advice was given by officers.
Caller stated a cougar had walked through the property. WILDCOMM provided advice.

DFW Officer received two reports, one of seeing two cougars and one of seeing one cougar, of cougars in the area.  DFW Officer spoke with both reporting parties and believe due to proximity that the sightings are related.

Reporting party had seen a cougar in his yard near his house.  DFW Officer discussed with RP what constitutes defense of self and property.  There are livestock on the property and cougar information was provided.

DFW Officers and Wildlife Conflict Specialist responded to a report of a sheep that was killed by an unknown animal.  After conducting a necropsy it was determined the trauma was consistent with a cougar attack.
Cougar was reported coming up to a house and looking in a window.
Cougar was spotted on a hill behind reporting party residence.  The cougar walked off and did not cause any issues.  RP had warned all of his neighbors.
Caller saw a cougar crossing through properties. Officers called and provided advice.
Caller advised her dog had been confronted by a cougar. There was a sighting near her residence and her dog had come home with puncture wounds that same day. Regional office gave her advice.
Caller had four sheep killed on her property. She stated that she hadn't seen the predator but it dug under her fence. Officers called the homeowner and placed a game camera on her property.
Caller advised of a deceased deer that had been eaten on. They assumed it was killed by a cougar. Officers were not able to confirm this.
Caller advised that two employees had been chased into a building by 2 cougar. Officers spoke to security who was unclear of all the details. It was likely a bobcat not a cougar based on location.
Caller advised a cougar was seen that they thought had killed a deer. Officers responded and found no evidence supporting this claim.
Caller had a goat killed in his dog kennel. He thought a cougar was responsible. Unconfirmed.

Caller reported a pig and miniature horse attacked on his property by what he believes was a cougar. Officers called and were told that no one had actually seen a cougar but the information provided originally was based off of the callers experience in Montana. Officers and biologist looked at images provided and could not confirm it was a cougar.
Caller saw a cougar walking in the yard that had previously killed 7 chickens. Officers provided advice.

Report of four horses with claw marks on the rear area of the animals and one deceased from a bite or heart attack.  DFW Officers used hounds to try and locate signs of a cougar but where unable to locate the animal.

Cougar was reported to DFW that was running down an alley way.  The reporting party has seen other cougars and wanted to report the cougar as they understood that DFW was try to keep track of the locations of the local cougars.
Caller reported a cougar near their property by their chicken coop. Officers called and provided advice after finding out it was a deer eating their bushes.

While horseback riding with her dog behind their house a cougar attacked the dog.  Others were able to fire shots into the bushed where the animals were fighting.  DFW Officers were not able to locate the cat after searching the area.
Caller advised there were injuries to her pony. Officers responded and verified the attack was canine.
Caller advised a cougar had been in the area preying on domestic cats. Officers provided information. Unconfirmed.
Caller advised a goat was killed. Officers and hounds responded but were unable to locate a cougar scent. Advice was provided.

Reporting party's son observed a cougar walking across the road during the morning hours.  They also reported there was a half eaten deer in the area.  DFW Officer advised them to view the information on the WDFW Living with Wildlife website.

DFW Officer was contacted in reference to a cougar that was killed by dogs in an orchard that is fenced in by a ten foot tall fence.  Officer informed reporting party to leave the carcass in place and it would be collected by a DFW official.
Cougar was reported in the area.  DFW Officer confirmed the sighting and was not able to locate the cat.
Caller saw a cougar cross through a field. Officers provided advice.
Caller had a cougar walk through their yard. Advice was provided.
Caller advised looking for information on a black cougar that had been posted on nextdoor app. Officers called and provided information. Unconfirmed.
Caller reported a cougar walked through the property. Officers tried calling back but got no answer.
Caller advised one of his goats had been attacked and killed by an unknown predator. Officers called and were unable to determine was had killed it. The caller set up game cameras.

DFW Officers received a report of a cougar that was bedded down in a green belt area.  DFW Officers responded with immobilization kits in an attempt to relocate the cougar that had multiple reports of being sighted.  The cat was not located.

DFW Officer was contacted in reference to a recently killed sheep.  Officer confirmed it was a cougar that killed the sheep, hounds were used in an attempt to locate the cougar but they were unable to locate the cat.

Reporting party contacted DFW reporting a sheep depredation that was most likely due to a cougar.  DFW Officer responded and confirmed the wounds were consistent with a cougar.  Hounds were used but were unable to locate the cat.  A camera was set up

Reporting party reported a cougar in the area.  DFW Officer contacted RP and they discussed how there is a natural area nearby and wildlife will always be there.  Advised them to view the living with wildlife webpage for information.
Reporting party reported a cougar in their yard.  The cougar was seen moving north bound on Adams Street from 16th Ave.

Reporting party saw a cougar in his yard around 2200 hours.  RP reported the cougar trotted through his back yard and jumped over a fence.  DFW Officers advised RP to keep his pets indoor for the night.

Reporting party contacted DFW reporting he killed a cougar the previous night that was coming after his sheep.  RP has had sheep killed in the past.  DFW Officer responded and confirmed the report, collected and disposed of the carcass.

Reporting party contacted DFW to report he had two sheep killed and another injured by a possible cougar.  The two dead sheep had a crushed windpipe and other injuries consistent with a cougar.  There was no signs of entry into the fenced area.
Caller reported cougar walking down the street. Officers called providing advice.
Caller reported hearing a cougar outside her home. Officers provided information.
Caller advised her young daughter saw a cougar while playing outside. Officers called the citizen back and provided advice.
Caller reported a cougar killed two chickens that belonged to his neighbor. Officers called and provided information.

Reporting party found a dead coyote on their property that had wounds consistent with a cougar.  DFW Officers and conflict specialist viewed photos that were consistent with what a cougar may do.  Later RP saw a cat leaving the area of the carcass.
Caller advised a cougar killed a deer in their area. Officers called and provided advice.
Caller advised a cougar was seen in a nearby field. Officers provided advice.
Caller reported a cougar taking their chickens. Advice was given by officers.

DFW Officer was contacted in reference to a ram killed by a possible cougar.  DFW Officer responded, confirmed a fresh kill, and used a hounds men to attempt to find the cat.  Unable to locate and a camera did not capture any photos during the night.

DFW Officer was contacted by a hounds man who was told about a cougar that was in a residents back yard attempting to get at a house cat through a screen window.  The cougar ran off when the resident went outside to confront the cat.

DFW Officers responded to a cougar that had been shot inside a chicken coop.  Officer confirmed the cougar had been killed in the act of depredation of poultry.  Officer provided information on reporting requirements and ways to prevent conflicts.
Caller saw a cougar walk through the property. Officers contacted and provided advice.

DFW Officer received report of a cougar in a field.  Officer responded to area and was unable to locate the cat.  A hounds man was used and the dogs hit on spots but had no continuous trail.  DFW Officer spoke with residents in the area.

A cougar had been seen in the area on several occasions.  Residents had fired warning shots at the cat.  The cat kept returning on different days.  A neighbor had shot the cat when his dog alerted to the cat and the cat was coming toward them.
Caller advised a cougar walked through the orchard. There were workers in the field that saw it. Officers provided advice.
Caller advised that a cougar killed a deer. Officers provided information.
Caller saw a cougar behind his property. This was unconfirmed.
Caller had a sheep killed by a cougar. Officers responded and confirmed it was likely killed by a cougar but the trap was unsuccessful.
Caller's son saw a cougar that morning walking down the street. This is the second sighting for the area. Officers drove through unable to find anything.

DFW Officer received report of a warning shot being fired at a cougar that had come near a camp site.  Officer responded and discussed the events with the party, provided advice on techniques that could be used to scare cougars off and safety issues.
Caller advised their neighbor had a cougar in their yard. Officers provided advice.
Caller advised a fawn was killed in his yard by a cougar. Officers called and provided advice.
Caller advised her neighbor saw a cougar near her residence. Officers provided advice.

DFW Officer received a report of an alpacas being harvested by a cougar.  Description of the wounds and were the animal fed on the carcass were consistent with a cougar.  Advice was provided to the owner.
Caller advised a dog had gotten killed. Officers responded and verified that the caller only heard a loud noise and hadn't actually seen a dog get taken. Unconfirmed.
Caller advised that their dog had been killed. Officers responded and found a 100 pound newfoundland deceased. The scene and evidence pointed to the culprit being coyotes.
A miniature horse was reported as being harvested by a cougar.  DFW Officers responded and set a trap with a trail camera.

DFW Officer responded to a report of four sheep and several cats being lost to a cougar.  The carcasses were fed on in a way that was consistent with a cougar.  Advice and information was provided to the resident.
Caller advised his neighbor saw a cougar. Officers provided advice.
Caller advised that a cougar killed a deer late on the night of 8/10/2017. Officers provided advice.

DFW Officer responded to a report of a cougar harvesting two donkeys.  Officer met with owner who showed him the two carcasses, one which was cashed and was fed on.  Officer set a trap on the location of one of the carcasses and captured a cougar.

Caller advised her horse had wounds from what she thought was a cougar confrontation. Officers responded and did not find tracks for the cougar and verified the markings were not consistent with a cougar attack.
Caller advised he shot a cougar that was attacking his sheep. Officers responded and confirmed the depredation.

DFW Officers received a report of a cougar acting strange.  The owner had scared the cat off but when it returned he thought it was coming at him and shot in defense of himself.  The cougar was located by hounds, was injured, and was euthanized.

Caller advised his horse had injuries or markings from a possible confrontation with a cougar. Officers responded to look at the horse and did not find the marks consistent with a cougar confrontation.
Caller reported a cougar walking through the area.

DFW Officer received report of a cougar attempting to take one chicken.  Homeowners yelled at the cougar which dropped the chicken and the chicken ran off.  A cougar had been spotted previously at night in a field a week ago.

Landowner observed a cougar jump into his pen that houses his turkeys and harvest one.  Owners dog treed a cougar where he shot the cougar.  DFW Officer responded to confirm the cougar and remove the carcass.
Caller advised of a cougar sighting across the roadway. She had lost three goats one week ago and a turkey. Officer provided information.

DFW Officer responded to a report of a dead sheep.  The wounds and condition of the sheep were consistent with those caused by a cougar.  A trap was set and hounds were used in an attempt to locate the cougar, both were unsuccessful.

DFW Officer received a report of an individual that was being stalked by a cougar in the Rock Creek area.  Person did not feel safe walking back to their vehicle.  Officers responded and contacted the person on a forest road in his vehicle.
A WSP trooper saw a cougar cross the road and go towards the riverside.
A WSP Trooper saw a cougar run under the bridge on highway 153 at MP19

DFW Officer received report of a cougar that was seen running off to the south or east.  A relative of the homeowner observed the cougar harvest their domestic cat.  Cougar was not able to be located.
Caller advised of a cougar that crossed the roadway near their campsite.

Advised of seeing a cougar at Blodgett and Anderson Rd just after midnight.  Second report of seeing a large cougar at 14th and Blackburn around 6AM.  Both RP's when interviewed gave very detailed descriptions and indicated there was a long tail.

Caller reported a sheep depredated by a cougar a few years ago. His neighbor had seen one that morning and was worried they would attack his livestock. Officers responded to the residence where it was observed but couldn't confirm.
Caller advised he and his wife were on a walk when they saw eyes glowing in the grass. Officers provided advice. Unconfirmed.
Caller advised of a cougar sighting in the woods. Officers tried calling back to provide information.

Owner reported seeing a cougar chasing coyotes and their dog.  The next night a deer came into their yard and a cougar was paralleling the deer.  Advice was given on cougar behavior and timely reporting.
Caller witnessed a cougar take one of his chickens. Officers called and verified it was likely a bobcat that was responsible.
Caller advised a cougar on his property killed his cat. Officers called and provided advice.

Report of a cougar that had a deer on the ground.  The cougar ran off when reporting party went outside to look at what was causing all the noise.  DFW Officer provided advice on cougar behavior and right to protect self and pets from a cougar.

Landowner reported he lost 5 sheep and 5 more are missing.  The sheep had puncture bite wounds in the neck that are three inches wide.  He has improved his fencing and pen area to attempt to keep the cougar out.

Caller reported that a cougar had been attacking her sheep over the last week. Officers responded with conflict staff and after looking at the lamb carcass confirmed it wasn't a cougar kill. Officers confirmed coyote were responsible.
Caller reported losing house cats in the last month. They had seen a predator chasing their domestic cat and walked outside to see a cougar following it. The subject shot the cougar in self defense.
Caller advised he saw a cougar walk across the driveway.

DFW Officer responded to report of a sheep harvested by a cougar.  The wounds on the sheep were consistent with those made by a cougar.  The landowner was able to watch over the carcass and euthanize the cougar when it returned to feed on the sheep.

DFW Officer responded to call of three sheep being harvested by a cougar.  The three sheep showed signs of being harvested by a cougar, a trap and camera were set.  The cougar did return and was seen on the camera but did not spring the trap.
Caller reported that a cougar killed his mother in laws dogs that were used to guard livestock. The dog had been drug down to a creek and buried.
Caller advised a cougar was in a tree near his residence. Officers responded and checked the area. Two houndsmen were called to the residence but did not strike on a cougars scent.
Caller lost a dog to a suspected cougar. Officers and houndsmen responded but the dogs had no hit on cougar. A depredation permit was issued.

Landowner reported a cougar that was walking across the property.  Reporting party believed a cougar had taken some ducks weeks ago and now it was back.  Officer discussed cougar behavior and that cougars rarely stay in the same area that long.

Home owner reported a cougar came to her back porch at night and was looking through the patio doors.  Owner has a dog that was inside.  DFW Officer determined the weather and passage of time made it not feasible for hounds to track the cougar.
Caller reported a cougar killed a deer 50 feet from her door. Officers called and provided advice. The deer appeared to have been killed by a domestic dog.
Caller advised she hit a cougar with her car. The cat ran off. Officers called and provided advice.

DFW Officer received a report of a cougar that had attacked a dog and was fought off by the owner.  The attacked occurred one day prior and the heat made it too late to attempt to track the cougar.  Advice on contacting DFW immediately was given.
Caller advised they saw a cougar at 1100 hours.

Caller advised one of her goats had been killed by a cougar. Officers responded and confirmed the culprit to likely be a cougar. Officers called a houndsman to respond and locate the cougar but were unsuccessful. The houndsman was issued a depredation permit.

Caller advised a cougar was in her yard after killing a goat.. Officers contacted a houndsman to respond and confirmed the goat was killed by a cougar. Houndsman helped treed the cat where it was lethally removed by officers.
Caller found cougar scat in his yard. Officers responded and found it to be house cat scat.
Caller advised he saw a cougar. It had been in the bushes watching them near the creek. Officers called and provided advice.

Caller advised there was a cougar sighting on their property. When officers contacted the caller they stated a dog had been killed earlier this week. Officers were unable to find a houndsman to come out.
Caller reported hearing a growling by her goat pen.. She saw no animals but thought it could have been a cougar. Officers called and provided advice.
Caller advised he saw a cougar on the trail ahead of him. He yelled and the cougar ran off.
Caller saw a cougar jump a fence into a neighbors yard. Officers called and provided advice.
Caller advised of a cougar print found in the area. Officers were unable to confirm.
DFW Officer advised resident of his rights concerning a cougar that came into his yard as he was letting his dog in the house.  The cougar came down and waited outside for ten minutes before leaving.

Caller advised her horse was found deceased with puncture marks on it's shoulder. Officers responded and found only one wound post mortem on the top of the right shoulder. It was determined by all parties to have died of natural causes.
Caller lost three lambs last year to a cougar and thought it had returned. He found scratch marks on his trees. Officers responded to the residence and found the scratch marks too low to be a cougar.

Home owner reported seeing a cougar run across the hillside behind her house in the morning.  DFW Officer advised a hound hunter who will attempt to track down a cougar.  Area will be monitored for additional cougar activity.
Caller advised he saw a cougar take down a deer. He heard a cry and when he looked over the bank saw what he thought was a cougar pinning a deer to the ground. He yelled and the cougar took off.

DFW Officer received a report of a cougar harvesting a goat.  Too much of the goat had been eaten to set a trap.  On 09/11/2017 the cougar had returned and killed another goat before the landowner was able to dispatch the cougar.

CALLER REPORTED A POSSIBLE ATTACK ON HER HORSE BY WHAT SHE THOUGHT WAS A COUGAR. THE HORSE SURVIVED BUT HAD CLAW MARKS AND PUNCTURE WOUNDS. OFFICERS REVIEWED IMAGES OF THE INJURIES AND DETERMINED IT WAS NOT FROM A COUGAR.
Caller advised a cougar ran across the roadway in front of his vehicle. Advice was provided.
Caller advised of a cougar sighting. Officers called the citizen reporting and provided her advice for her livestock.
CALLER WITNESSED A COUGAR TAKE DOWN A DEER. OFFICERS CALLED AND PROVIDED ADVICE.
Caller reported that his tenant at a rental property witnessed a cougar take her cat the week before. Officers called and provided advice.
Caller reported a cougar in his yard. It was the third sighting in the neighborhood. Officers called and provided legal advice.
Caller advised of a cougar in his backyard. He was concerned it had not left and that children lived in the area. Officers called and provided advice.
CALLER OWNS AN APARTMENT COMPLEX AND AN ELDERLY RESIDENT INFORMED HER THAT THEY HAVE SEEN A COUGAR IN THE PARKING LOT THE LAST TWO NIGHTS. ADVICE WAS GIVEN BY WILDCOMM.
Lincoln County sheriff responded to a call of a cougar treed by the homeowners dogs.  Sheriff arrived and was able to dispatch the cougar.  DFW Officer arrived and recovered the carcass.

CALLER REPORTED A COUGAR KILL.  OFFICERS RESPONDED AND CONFIRMED. OFFICERS WENT TO THE RESIDENCE WITH A HOUND HUNTER TO FIND AND HUMANELY EUTHANIZE THE COUGAR. OFFICERS RESPONDED THE NEXT DAY WITH HOUNDS AND TREED A LARGE MALE COUGAR NEAR THE RESIDENCE. THE COUGAR WAS REMOVED BY OFFICERS.
CALLER CONTACTED WSP TO REPORT A COUGAR SIGHTING. UNCONFIRMED.
Caller advised she heard a cougar near her house at 10:30 PM. This was the second time it had been heard. Officers called and provided advice.

DFW Officer responded to a report of a cougar attacking a dog.  The dog was taken to a vet where a puncture wound was found.  Three days later a report of 2 goats possibly taken by a cougar was confirmed.  A cougar was trapped and euthanized.
Caller advised of 2 sheep killed that she thought was due to a cougar. Officers called and left a VM but never heard back.

DFW Officer responded to a report of a cougar killing a sheep.  Land owner found a sheep carcass that had been dragged into a swamp area.  The carcass was too old and the weather too hot to use hounds to try and locate the cougar.

Caller advised hearing loud thumps on her roof. She heard a screaming/crying sound as well. Her neighbor told her that three cougars had been seen in the area recently. She thought the thump on her roof was a cougar. Officers called providing advice.
Caller lost four goats to a cougar. Officers confirmed this with prints taken by the citizen who owned the goat. Officers issued a depredation permit to a hound hunter.
DFW Officer received a report of a cougar being seen on multiple occasions.  The cougar did not appear to be scared off by people or passing cars.  Officer provided advice to reporting party.

Caller advised of a possible cougar sighting in her neighborhood. On 9/12/2017 her 15 year old son saw what he thought was a cougar in their driveway. Officers asked for video but due to quality were not able to confirm it.
Caller advised of a cougar in his backyard. Officers provided advice.
Caller advised a cougar was in her yard. She had gone outside to get her dog and cat when the cougar ran towards her vehicle parked in the driveway. The caller went back inside and called 911.
Caller advised there was a cougar coming onto her property. She also had found a deer buried on her property. Officers contacted her and provided advice.
Caller advised a cougar was captured on trail camera on 8/25/2017.

DFW Officer received a report of two sheep being killed by a cougar.  Biologist examined the carcasses and set up a trail camera which captured images of a cougar with two kittens.  Officers and biologists will determine the best strategy to take.
Caller saw a cougar on his property. He fired a warning shot at the cougar and it left. Advice was provided by officers.
Caller advised one of the security guards at the school saw a cougar near the property. Officers responded to the area and did a sweep and were unable to locate a cougar or any signs of one.
Caller advised of a cougar sighting behind the apartment complex. She had seen green glowing eyes from her backdoor and light colored hair. Officers provided advice.

DFW Officer was notified of a house cat that was possibly killed by a cougar.  The cat was found in pieces in the backyard by the homeowner.  There were reports of a possible cougar in the area.  A hound dog was used but could not locate a cougar.
Caller had seen a cougar walking through a neighborhood near Pittsburgh Street and West Victoria Avenue in Kennewick.

DFW Officer received a report of a cougar being killed by landowner while the cougar was in a chicken coup.  Owner said the cougar had killed four chickens before owner shot the cougar.  Officer inspected the site and confirmed the information.
Caller advised of a cougar sighting at her residence. Officers called the citizen and were told it was 16 feet from her residence. Advice was given.

DFW Officers received a report of an Alpaca that was harvested by a cougar.  The Alpaca had bite marks on throat and was fed on in ways that were consistent with a cougar.  Camera set up on carcass and the cougar did not return.
Caller advised he had five goats missing and one more dying in his enclosure. It was not confirmed to have been a cougar depredation and was likely coyotes.

Caller advised that a fawn was found in his yard eaten by what he thought was cougar. Officers called the citizen and based on the information provided sounded more like coyote involvement rather than cougar.
Cougar was seen at night.  Previously a month and a half ago a cougar was also spotted.  DFW Officer provided advice on actions to take if the cougar was seen again.
Cougar sighting- unconfirmed.
Caller advised of a cougar sighting the night before. Officers called for further information. The cougar had been seen on the property on multiple occasions. Officers provided advice.

Caller advised his horse had scratch marks on it's neck. Due to the fact that a neighbor saw a cougar in the area he presumed that was the culprit. Officers responded and put up a trail camera but neither they or the vet could confirm that a cougar was responsible.
Caller advised they lost their weiner dog after letting it out to use the bathroom the night prior. Officers called the citizen and he advised her ended up finding his dog at the nearby school.
Caller advised of a cougar sighting behind the Shell Station near Winlock.
Caller advised of a dead goat. Officers responded and based on evidence found the culprit to be coyote.

Caller reported one duck had been killed inside a fenced area with about 4 foot fence. One duck was later recovered alive and missing some tail feathers. The dead duck had been partially eaten inside the pen by what appeared to be a much smaller predator than a cougar.  She said the cougar had black around its eyes and had a white muzzle. Officers checked the area and found no evidence of cougar.
Caller advised some of her livestock had been attacked and killed. Officers responded with conflict staff and determined the predator  to be domestic canine.
Caller advised his mother's dog was attacked by a cougar the Thursday prior. Officers contacted and provided advice as it was not confirmed.
Caller reported three sightings of a cougar in their area. They had never seen it but wanted it reported.
Caller advised that his daughter lost three sheep in three weeks. Officers called and provided advice.
Caller reported a lamb on her property taken by a cougar. Officers contacted the citizen back but they advised they didn't want any action taken.
A cougar was believed to be responsible for injuring a mini horse and pony on two separate properties.  Owners of the pony provided photographs showing the injuries that were found on their pony.

DFW Officer responded to a report of a cougar under a porch.  The cougar was there the night prior, Officer found evidence of blood and hair that was consistent with a depredation.  Officer provided reporting party with advice and contact numbers.
Caller reported a cougar sighting on the property.
Caller reported an ongoing problem with deer killed by cougar in their backyard. Officers responded and verified it was likely killed by bobcat not a cougar.

Caller reported a cougar on their property with increasing frequency. They believed it had killed one of their goats previously as it was never located. They also had seen it approx. 15 feet from them one day while outside. Officers called and provided advice.
Caller saw a cougar walking towards her address. Officers called and provided advice.
Caller reported seeing a cougar across the highway from his backyard.
Caller advised that a cougar crossed the roadway. Callers husband saw it at 0930 hours. It was unconfirmed.

Owner reported he found five carcasses, later updated to six, of livestock that were harvested by an unknown animal.  The injuries were consistent with that of a cougar.  DFW Officer provided advice on keeping the animals secure and contact numbers.
Caller reported a large feline laying in the grass next to a walking trail. Officers responded and were unable to locate any large cats.
Homeowner reported depredation of five sheep and one llama.  The wounds were to the head and neck and claw marks on the backs.

Concerned that a bobcat or mountain lion is taking livestock. He has had problems in the past of coyotes attacking goats during daytime, but he has had multiple kid goats completely disappear during the night. One of his adult females was also attacked about a month ago, but his dogs alerted him in time to save her. She suffered puncture wounds to head and neck. Officers believe it was either coyotes or bobcats.
Caller advised there was a depredation on a calf.
Caller advised that a cougar had a confrontation with his dogs- This was the second instance in 2 weeks.

A cougar had harvested two goats on the property.  DFW Officers contacted a hound hunter to attempt to locate the cougar but were notified the cougar had returned to feed on the goat carcasses and the owner had harvested the cougar.

DFW Officer received a report of a cougar that came out from under a porch with a chicken.  DFW Officers responded where they were told the landowner's son had seen a cougar with a chicken being taken away.  A hound hunter was issued a permit.

DFW Officers were notified of a possible depredation of a sheep.  DFW Officers responded and confirmed the sheep had been harvested by a cougar.  There were bite marks to the neck which was also broken.  A houndsman was used but could not locate.

CALLER ADVISED OF A COUGAR SIGHTING ON HER PROPERTY.  SHE DESCRIBED THE COUGAR AND STATED THAT THE ANIMAL HAD BEEN SITTING A SHORT DISTANCE FROM HER HOUSE.  DEPUTIES WERE ABLE TO RESPOND QUICKLY AND SEARCHED THE AREA BUT WERE NOT ABLE TO SEE THE ANIMAL
Caller reports that he saw a cougar cross the road near his house. Officers called and provided advice.
Recieved a report via Aberdeen PD of a possible Cougar sighting near the Robert Gray middle school located on B street in Aberdeen. Officers responded but were unable to locate any signs of a cougar.
Caller reported a deer killed on his property. Officers contacted him and advised he could dispose of it.
