Citizen reported sighting a possible cougar on his property. WDFW is unable to confirm the sighting at this time but provided advice.

Citizen reported four goats being killed by a possible cougar. WDFW investigated and found the puncture wounds on the goats were consistent with a cougar kill. A houndsman was called, the cougar was treed and euthanized.

Caller reported a sheep killed in his pasture. Officers responded to the area where they were told the sheep was found against a fence partially fed on. The same caller had lost two mini goats the month prior. Officers believe it could have been a cougar but the carcass had already been buried.
Citizen reported sighting a possible cougar on his sister's property on Tuesday. WDFW is unable to confirm the sighting at this time.

Citizen reported multiple goats being killed by a possible cougar. WDFW called out a houndsman but a cougar was not initially located due to the the report happening too long after the initial incident. Two days after the initial response, another livestock kill was reported on the same road. WDFW euthanized one cougar and the stomach content showed evidence of goats and it is presumed to be the same cougar that caused depredations days prior.
Citizen reported a deer carcass on her property that was killed by an unknown animal. WDFW is unable to confirm the cause at this time.
Citizen reported a cougar killing their sheep. WDFW determined from the carcass that the cause of death was a cougar and contacted a houndsman. The cougar was euthanized and removed.

Citizen reported to state patrol about being chased by possible cougars in his backyard and spraying them with a hose to scare them off. WDFW investigated and found no paw prints and based on the citizen's description, do not believe the cause to have been cougars.
Citizen reported a neighbor sighting a possible cougar in the citizen's yard the night prior in a tree around 11 pm. WDFW is unable to confirm the sighting at this time.

Citizen reported finding a deceased deer on the back of their property and believed the cause to have been from a cougar. WDFW investigated and believe the cause of death was either a coyote or vehicle kill.
Citizen reported sighting a cougar on Weyerhauser property near his residence. Citizen provided an accurate description of a cougar so WDFW confirmed it to be a plausible cougar sighting.

Caller reported walking in the wooded area. His truck had gotten stuck and he was walking near Parker Lake. He had been startled by a sound and ended up slipping on the ice. That is when he saw a cougar 5-8 feet from him. The cougar ran off when he went to grab his rifle.

Caller reported finding a dead deer in the bushes near his driveway. He stated that eagles had fed on it but he thought it was a cougar kill based on the placement into the bushes. WILDCOMM provided advice.

Caller reported that a cougar took one of her goats on friday. The goat was found missing it's head and was found in the woods. Officers called and verified it likely was a cougar kill however her husband was the one that moved the goat into the woods to prevent scavengers. There was not much left to go off of.

Caller reported a cougar that has been in their area for the last year or two. He had video of it breaking into a coop and killing two chickens. Officers called and provided general advice of securing his coop. The last image was on March 10th.
Caller reported a cougar captured on his RING camera. He was provided advice by WILDCOMM dispatch.

Caller reported a horse attacked by a cougar. Officers responded after receiving images of the horse. The officer believed after inspection that the wounds were caused by barbed wire. He walked the fenceline and found hair in a certain portion of the fence that fit the same height as the wounds on the horse. A deer had been freshly killed in the area however that he did believed to have been cached by a cougar. He set cameras.

Caller reported that three cougar were on his property the night prior trying to get into his turkey pen. The RP states he came out an hour later and saw the cougar near his pen crouched down so he shot and killed it. He stated the other two cougar had come back later to try and get back into his coop. He had stored the cougar in his neighbor's freezer.
Caller reported a neighbor showed him video of a large cougar that had been at their house four days prior. Officers attempted to call him back but were unable to reach him.
Caller reported a cougar that was spotted by her daughter. It had pointed ears with a very large tail.
Caller reported a cougar sighting in their area. An officer responded to check the location but was unable to find a cougar.
RP called and left a voicemail reporting seeing either a cougar or a bobcat the night prior.
Caller advised of a cougar sighting. An officer called and was told the cougar crossed the roadway.
Caller reported a cougar sighting on their property. Officers called and were told the cougar simply walked through her property and left without incident.

Citizen reported a possible cougar killing one of his sheep as well as some missing lambs. WDFW investigated and found the kill wounds were consistent with a cougar attack. WDFW issued a depredation permit to a houndsman for removal of one cougar.
Citizen reported a cougar killing his chickens and turkeys. Citizen provided picture of a cougar with a turkey in it's mouth. WDFW set a trap and baited it with one of the turkey carcasses.

Caller reported a cougar that took one of his turkeys. Officers responded and were shown pictures of a cougar. They set a bear trap and baited it with a turkey carcass. Caller reported that two days later the cougar returned and was trying to get into his coop again when he shot it. Conflict staff responded to get the carcass.
Caller reported second hand information of a cougar seen in a nearby park. Officers called and verified it likely was NOT a cougar.
Citizen reported an increase in cougar sightings in the area. WDFW is unable to confirm the sightings at this time.

Citizens believe they were being followed by cougars on their hike. WDFW officers came out to check on hikers and officers can not definitively determine if the animals that they hikers saw were cougars and they did not act aggressively.

Caller reported a cougar that took his chickens. Officers responded with conflict staff to investigate. Officers called hound hunters to respond as well based on carcasses found on scene. The hounds located and treed an adult female. Officers humanely euthanized the cougar and removed it from the property.

Caller reported a cougar that had been eating their cats.. It was caught on their trail camera close to their residence.  Officers called and left a voicemail. The caller reported that he found the carcass of one of his cats and then set up a trail camera where he saw the cougar. He had no evidence to believe that the cougar was the culprit.
Caller reported seeing a black cougar that passed through her yard. It was going towards a greenbelt behind her residence.

Caller reported his girlfriend saw a cougar in the canyon while walking the day prior at 11:45 hours. Her only concern was that when it saw her it proceeded to continue walking in her direction. Officers called and provided advice.
Caller reported a couar sighting in their driveway at 2000 hours on 4/4/2021. Conflict staff provided advice.
Citizen reported a possible cougar sighting. WDFW followed up with citizen and he states he thinks he might have seen a neighbors dog.
Citizen reported a possible cougar killing 6 chickens and 2 ducks. WDFW followed up but is unable to confirm sighting at this time.
Citizen reported sighting a possible cougar on their property edge the night prior.
Caller left a voicemail stating he saw a cougar in his yard the night prior. WILDCOMM attempted to contact him for more information but were unsuccessful.

Citizen reported 6 llamas being killed by a possible cougar, the most recent being one on Tuesday night. The carcass was already buried at time of report so WDFW could not evaluate carcass for cause of death.
Citizen reported a possible cougar. WDFW investigated and found no evidence of a cougar in the area.
Citizen reported to State Patrol possibly sighting a cougar cross the roadway. WDFW is unable to confirm the sighting at this time.

Caller reported a fresh cougar kill of a deer on their property. Officers called and responded to the area. The animal had been mostly eaten with the intestines removed with minimal disturbance. Officers could find no tracks. Officers provided advice on living in cougar territory.
Caller reported cougar activity in the area. There was a family of four cougar that was seen the week prior. WILDCOMM provided advice.

Caller advised two of her dwarf goats were killed. One was missing the other was laying nearby.  Officers responded and set a trap. They caught the cougar on 4/12 and it was an 8-9 year old female that had a green ear tag. The cat had history of depredation situations for years. Officers and conflict staff euthanized the cat.
Caller reported a cougar on their trail camera on the night of 4/11. It returned again on 4/12 and their small dog was taken. WILDCOMM provided advice.
Caller reported a cougar on the trail towards the baseball fields, She did not request a call back.
Caller reported a cougar frequenting their area that had been caught on camera. Officers called and provided advice.
Caller reported numerous videos of a cougar caught on camera. Caller stated she had this problem for many years.
Caller advised that a cougar walked through their property. Caller reports that his wife saw it leaving the property.
Caller reported seeing a cougar walking along the sidewalk. It was 20 feet from her window and had a large tail. Officers provided advice.

Citizen reported sighting two possible cougars in the park area. WDFW contacted a houndsman in the area. Houndsman advised the dogs detected a cougar scent. A person in the park advised the houndsman he had seen the two cougars walking in opposite directions.
Citizen reported sighting a cougar that killed two coyotes on their property. WDFW provided advice on cougar behavior.
Citizen reported a secondhand sighting of someone sighting a cougar near the school. WDFW Called and provided advice to the school.
Citizen reported cougars frequenting the area and caught on game cameras. WDFW has not confirmed the sightings at this time.
Caller advised of a cougar captured on his property. Officers provided advice.
Citizen reported sighting a cougar 2 days prior on their property. WDFW provided advice and is unable to confirm the sighting at this time.
Citizen reported sighting a possible cougar in the park that morning as well as a week prior.
Citizen reported a sheep doing missing due to a possible cougar. WDFW investigated and called out a houndsman. A cougar was not located and neither was a carcass of the sheep.
Citizen reported a possible cougar walking through the neighborhood. WDFW Advised that based on the description, it was not likely a cougar.
Caller reported a cougar sighting in the residential area of Leclerc Rd N And CEe Cee Ah Creek. It ran off when it saw the caller. Officers provided advice.
Citizen reported sighting a possible cougar multiple times in the area. WDFW is unable to confirm the sighting at this time.
Citizen reported that her dog scared a cougar up a tree while she was hiking. WDFW provided advice on hiking in cougar habitat.

Citizen reported a possible cougar walking through their property. WDFW responded and observed pictures that the citizen took. WDFW confirmed the pictures of the cougar, it was about 70 lb juvenile. The cougar disappeared onto timber property nearby. WDFW set up trail cameras.

Citizen reported to state patrol that they sighted a possible cougar near their chicken coop. WDFW officer investigated a neighboring property where the cougar was last spotted. WDFW could not locate a cougar but found a partial possible cougar print.
Citizen reported a cougar near their calf. Citizen submitted a picture as well. WDFW confirmed sighting and provided advice.
Caller reported that his tree crew saw a cougar walk between two homes while working. WILDCOMM provided advice.

Citizen reported their three sheep being killed by a possible cougar. WDFW concluded the depredation cause was a cougar. A houndsman was called but the dogs were unable to locate a cougar scent. WDFW issued a depredation permit for one month.
Citizen reported a possible cougar taking one of their sheep. WDFW is unable to locate the animal and are not able to confirm the cougar to be the cause at this time.
Caller reported a cougar seen by her neighbor crossing through her property. WILDCOMM provided advice.

Caller states that she had been seeing and hearing a cougar in the area of enchantment park (204 River St).  She did not state specific dates, but suggested the most recent may have been from the weekend. Officers called and provided advice.

The department received multiple reports of a cougar sighting or signs of a cougar in the area. One report stated it had a yellow ear tag. Officers hiked the area and were able to confirm that proper signage was placed but found no signs of a cougar itself.  Advice was provided and they will monitor the area.

Caller reported four cougars hanging out in the area.  Officers called and were told that the caller had not ever actually seen the cougar but one of their staff had. Officers reached out to a local houndsman and biologist regarding a study in the area. Officers provided advice and contact information.
Caller reported a cougar that was caught on his security camera. WILDCOMM provided advice.

Caller reported a cougar in their area. It was caught on a neighbor's camera and then another neighbor had reported it on NEXTDOOR being on his back porch. Images sent in confirmed it was a cougar. WILDCOMM provided advice.
Citizen reported sighting a collared cougar near his livestock. WDFW advised setting up a camera and advised of rights to protect himself and property.

Caller advised of a possible second cougar attack on his calves. Both had been left in tact and not pulled apart. Officers arrived at the residence and based on evidence of the scene it was likely not done by a cougar but rather coyotes. The animal had not been cached and their were no wounds to the neck or head.
Caller reported a large male cougar on their trail camera that has been frequenting the area for a month. Conflict staff called and provided advice as the cougar had not done anything unusual.
Caller reported a cougar that crossed their street heading south. WILDCOMM provided advice as the caller did not appear concerned.

Caller reported a cougar that killed one of his sheep. He was able to scare it off with warning shots. Officers arrived at the residence and were advised that two sheep had actually been killed. They caught an image of a cougar on their trail camera. Conflict staff and officers attempted to run hounds.
Citizen reported a goat being killed by a possible cougar. WDFW set up a cougar trap, trapped and euthanized cougar.
Cougar was caught on game camera and houndsman was called out to remove two subadult cougars
Citizen reported sighting a possible cougar in the park. WDFW is unable to confirm the sighting at this time.
Citizen reported a possible cougar chasing a neighbor's dog. WDFW provided advice.
Citizen reported sighting a cougar two days in a row near the golf course. WDFW is unable to confirm the sighting at this time.
Citizen reported sighting a possible cougar near his residence while walking his dog early in the morning. WDFW is unable to confirm the sighting at this time.
Citizen reported a cougar coming to her property. Citizen submitted video footage. WDFW confirmed it to likely be a cougar.
Caller reported a cougar that continued to come back and sit on his porch. Officers called and provided advice. The sighting is confirmed as the caller had experience trapping cougars with the USDA.
Caller reported a cougar that continued to come back and sit on his porch. Officers called and provided advice. The sighting is confirmed as the caller had experience trapping cougars with the USDA.

Caller reported her husband heard something run across their roof chasing something. Later in the morning she looked out and saw a cougar approx. 15 feet from her residence. Officers met with the caller and walked the residence but were unable to confirm it was a cougar based on no tracks.

Caller reported a cougar that killed several of his goats. Officers left a message for the caller. Officers responded and verifies that the wounds were consistent with a cougar kill. Officers were trying to set a trap but could not get landowner permission. They had to set a trap in another area but were unsuccessful.
Caller reported a cougar sighting in the hills behind his home. It was very wooded and uninhabited. Advice was given.
Caller reported a cougar seen in their front yard. It was seen around 6PM and was brightly colored with a long trail. It was last seen headed north. WILDCOMM provided advice.
Caller reported a cougar in the tree on their property. Officers called back and were told it was actually on a trail behind their property and was confirmed by photographs.
Caller reported two cougars observed in the area. One was in the trees and one was on the ground in the bushes. They were apparently growling at eachother.

Caller reported a cougar wandering in their livestock enclosure. Conflict staff contacted the homeowner and were told they had lost three to four sheep and goats over the last few nights and today were missing a calf. They had seen a collared cougar and two sub adult cougars in the area. Officers responded with hounds to the residence. They found the sub adult cougars and one female cougar. All three were lethally removed from the property.
Caller advised of a cougar that walked through her property at 1500 hours. It had been seen approximately four times in the area. WILDCOMM provided advice.

Caller advised that three of their sheep had been killed by a cougar. Officers responded to the location and were told two had been killed Tuesday and one on Wednesday morning. They were drug to the fence and then buried. Officers verified it was a cougar and set a trap with a trail camera.

Caller reported livestock killed by an unknown predator near where a deer was found deceased as well. They believed it to be a cougar. Officers responded and learned that the carcasses all had been disposed of. They showed officers pictures which confirmed the kill was likely domestic dogs as the carcasses were not fed on.
Caller reported a cougar that was caught on her back porch. It left after pacing back and forth. Officers provided advice.
Caller reported a cougar that she saw while running. She was unable to get a good look at the animal but described it as having pointed ears and being brown and grey. WILDCOMM provided advice.
Caller reported a cougar at the golf course the night prior. It was climbing a tree. Officers provided advice.

Caller reported a goat that went missing. Officers called and were told that one of the goats had gone missing but no carcass was located. He assumed it was a cougar based on sightings by neighbor's in the area. Officers provided advice.
Caller reported cougar sightings on their orchards. They had employees that have seen it near their small outbuilding and while walking the rows. WILDCOMM Provided advice.
Citizen reported a dead deer on their property that was killed by a possible cougar. WDFW is unable to confirm the sighting at this time.
Citizen reported a cougar on their camera late at night near their chicken coop. Citizen states the cougar was scared off by a motion light. WDFW provided advice.
Local police officer reported a cougar sighting in the area. WDFW referred the information to the Kalispel tribe to contribute to their cougar monitoring study.

Citizen reported sighting a cougar on their back porch to state patrol. WDFW investigated and found a cougar laying nearby with an ear tag. WDFW officer found that the cougar had previously been relocated but found its way back to town and was not concerned with people. WDFW removed the cougar.
Citizen reported a possible cougar sighting on their property. WDFW is unable to confirm the sighting at this time.
Citizen reported concerns of a possible cougar being in the area. WDFW is unable to confirm the sighting at this time.

Caller reported one deceased lamb he found on his property. The point of contact was the head and neck area. Another lamb was found injured but alive. Officers arrived on scene and called out hounds based on a necropsy performed. They were unable to track the cougar due to the time delay but set a trap.
Caller reported a cougar sighting on his property regularly. The last time it was seen was one month prior.

Caller reported a cougar that ran through their yard to WSP. Officers headed to the location and met with the citizen. Officers found a faint track that they believed to be cougar. Officers checked the area unable to find the cougar. They provided information to all of the neighbors and checked all of the schools in the area to provide information.

Caller reported a cougar under their porch. Officers called the citizen while enroute the resident and were advised that she was certain it was a cougar. Officers asked that county have a deputy respond as well. The deputy was unable to locate the cougar or any signs of one.

Caller reported a cougar that chased one of her dogs out of their goat pen and into her barn. Officers called and were headed to the property. RP states the owners dogs had killed a cougar kitten. Officers called and provided advice on future conflict.
Caller reported a cougar that crossed the road behind his vehicle. He was provided advice.
Caller reported that his neighbor saw a cougar jump out of the tree on their property and go into the ravine nearby. WILDCOMM provided him with advice.

Citizen reported multiple cougars around his property. County officer responded and found no evidence of cougars, but did see some free range chickens. WDFW talked to Kalispel Tribe to see if they wanted to check the area. Kalispel tribe responded with hounds, but the hounds located no scent of any cougars in the area. WDFW officer relayed the findings to the homeowner and provided advice.

Citizen reported sighting an adult and a juvenile cougar near her livestock. Citizen had seen them at night and the next morning chasing her cattle. WDFW officer provided advice on securing livestock to protect them.
Citizen reported sighting a possible cougar on her property. WDFW is unable to confirm the sighting at this time.
Citizen reported sighting a possible cougar on their property. WDFW provided advice.

Caller reported a cougar that killed their goat this morning. It was found in the corner of his field. Officers responded and set a trap that was checked the next day. There was no cougar captured so the trap was taken down. Officers have not heard back from the owner since then.
Citizen reported a possible cougar killing his goat. WDFW investigated and set a trap. The cougar did not return at this time so the trap was removed.
Citizen reported a possible cougar under their building. WDFW investigated and could not locate any sign of cougar activity.

Caller reported a lamb that was killed in their pen. Officers responded to the address and based on a necropsy believe the lamb was killed by a cougar. The property owner had two previous problems with cougar as well at his residence. Officers provided advice on securing his livestock.
Citizens reported two sightings to state patrol regarding a possible injured cougar in the area. WDFW is unable to confirm the sightings at this time.
Citizen reported sighting two cougars on the property. WDFW confirmed it to likely be cougars in the area.
Citizen reported sighting a possible cougar walking the hill near the school around 3 am. WDFW is unable to confirm the sighting at this time.
Citizen reported that a family member had sighted a possible cougar on their property. WDFW is unable to confirm the sighting at this time.
Citizen reported sighting a possible cougar around 0745 hours that day. WDFW is unable to confirm the sighting at this time.
Citizen reported sighting possible cougars on her game camera on May 1 and April 3rd. WDFW is unable to confirm the sightings at this time.
Citizen reported sighting a cougar around 2200 hours on Sunday cross the roadway headed east. WDFW is unable to confirm the sighting at this time.
Citizen reported sighting a possible cougar on his security camera walking across his deck. WDFW contacted citizen and was able to confirm the sighting.

Caller reported a dead sheep on his property. Officers arrived at the location and inspected the carcass. He determined it was likely a cougar kill. The officer called out hounds but were unsuccessful.

Caller reported a dog that had been attacked by a cougar. Conflict staff called and were told that air BnB guests were walking their dogs when they were charged by a cougar and the dog ran off. The dog was injured but not killed. Officers and conflict staff responded to the address that appeared consistent with a cougar. Property owners requested the cougar not be lethally removed.  The dogs were unable to locate a cougar.

Citizen reported a possible cougar on the other side of his fence in the green belt about 2 weeks ago. Citizen did not get a good look at the animal. WDFW is unable to confirm the sighting at this time.

CALLER ADVISED THAT ON MAY 11TH AT AROUND 10:45 PM, HER MOTION LIGHTS WENT ON AND SHE HEARD AN ANIMAL SQUEALING.  SHE LOOKED OUTSIDE AND SAW WHAT APPEARED TO BE A LARGE CAT WITH AN ANIMAL IN ITS MOUTH ON 2ND ST IN FRONT OF HER HOME. NEIGHBORS THAT SHE HAD SEEN A COUGAR ON THE PREVIOUS FRIDAY IN THE SAME AREA.  SHE ADDED THAT HER NEIGHBORS DOGS HAD BEEN ATTACKED BY A COUGAR THE YEAR PRIOR NEAR THE SAME SPOT. OFFICERS ADVISED CONFLICT STAFF.
Caller reported a cougar on his game camera at 2315 hours on the 9th. WILDCOMM provided advice.
Cougar approached USFS crew and hiker. Crew was able to scare cat away when animal was 10 feet away. Young animal, perhaps 2 years old.
Caller reported a cougar on his game camera the night prior at 2330 hours. WILDCOMM provided advice.
Caller reported three cougar kittens that came through his property the night prior. He found fresh tracks as well. WILDCOMM and officers provided advice.
Caller reported her neighbor saw a cougar twice on their ring camera. WILDCOMM provided advice.
Caller reported a cougar at the top of the trail. He was not able to see details because of how far away it was. WILDCOMM provided advice.
Caller reported a neighbor that caught 3 cougars on their cameras. WILDCOMM provided advice.

Caller reported a cougar sighting at a park in Napavine. Deputies responded as fish and wildlife was unavailable. Officers called the next day and were told that the subjects were walking when they saw what they saw what they thought was a cougar. They then ran back to their vehicle and turned the lights on. They could see glowing eyes. Officers called the responding deputy who found the animal to be a dog that the owner was playing fetch with.

Caller reported a depredation on two goats. Conflict staff called and advised he would be out the following day. The caller reported that five goats the following night had been killed. Officers arrived on scene with hounds to locate the cougar. The dogs were unable to physically locate the cougar so a trap and game camera were set. As of 5/14 the cougar was not captured in the trap or on camera.

Caller reported a cougar or bobcat killed two of their goats the night before in their fenced enclosure. One of them had wounds on their neck and the other had the intestines eaten. WILDCOMM provided advice.
Caller reported a sheep killed. Conflict staff responded and based on the evidence and carcass left believe coyotes were likely the culprit.
Caller reported that a neighbor caught a female cougar on his trail camera two nights prior. It was described as having a long dark tipped tail and pointed ears. WILDCOMM provided advice.
Caller reported a cougar in her front yard two nights prior. WILDCOMM provided advice.
Caller reported a cougar that was in his front yard the night prior. He clapped his hands and it walked away. WILDCOMM provided advice.
Caller reported that she found footage from April 15th and May 7th of a cougar near her back door at 2100 hours. WILDCOMM provided advice

Caller reported that he lost calves to an unknown predator. Conflict staff responded and found evidence of the calf being drug under the fence. They called out hounds and found a cached carcass. Officers arrived on scene when a cougar was treed and removed by officers.
Caller reported a cougar on their game camera multiple times over the last week close to their residence. Officers called and provided advice.

Caller reported a cougar attack on livestock. He had four goats and two chickens killed in the middle of the night. Conflict staff followed up and stated that the goats were dropped off at an abandoned marijuana farm with no husbandry. Conflict staff provided advice.  Days later the same caller reported that he had shot a cougar that had killed some of his goats. He had sat on one of the carcasses and waited for it to come back to it.

Caller reported two of her goats killed by a cougar the night prior. THey were found buried in their pen after being drug a short distance. Officers responded and set a trap. They found evidence that it was likely a cougar kill.
Caller reported a cougar that he saw stalking his horse. Conflict staff called and provided advice.
Caller reported a cougar took his young goat through his fence the night prior. Officers called and provided advice.
Citizen reported a possible cougar on their property. WDFW is unable to confirm the sighting at this time.

Citizen reported three goats being killed by a possible cougar. Citizen later observed three cougars in the goat pen. Citizen fired a few shots and located one dead cougar. WDFW responded and located another dead cougar.

Caller reported a cougar depredation on one of her goats. Officers advised they needed to see the goat carcass to confirm what killed it. They did not have the carcass and were told to contact the officer back should they find it. Later that day a deputy found the carcass. Officers were later told that a hound with dogs found and removed the cougar.

Caller reported a cougar depredation the previous Sunday on two goats. Officers responded and found two goats in the pen. He found no tracks so he examined the goats. One appeared to have no visible injuries. The second was partially consumed and had wounds consistent with a cougar. Officers called hound hunters to try and locate it but he declined to respond. Officers set a trap instead and the next day caught the cougar. It was removed and euthanized.
Citizens reported cougar sightings in the area. WDFW investigated and confirmed it to likely be a cougar in the area.

Caller reported they had a goat killed by a cougar. Officers arrived on scene and located the goat . They found blood but no tracks of a cougar. The goat had been partially skinned and fed on. Officers found bite marks and a crushed esophagus indicating it was a cougar kill. They issued a depredation permit for the next seven days. The hounds man responded and tree the cougar where it was dispatched and removed.

Caller reported a cougar depredation that occurred Sunday night on two goats. Officers called and responded to the property. Officers did not locate any tracks in the area so she examined the goats. Officers noticed the throat had no bruising but did find a puncture near the eye.

Caller reported two of his goats that were attacked and killed with one missing. Officers arrived at the address and met with the landowner. They showed him the goat pen were two of the three goats were deceased. He examined them both and found wounds around the neckline consistent with cougar. Officers contacted hounds to search for the last carcass. The dogs were able to locate and adult female cougar in the tree- Officers lethally removed her.

Caller reported a large cougar he saw while target shooting. He reports that the cougar took steps towards him so he fired a warning shot. The cougar turned broadside before taking a few more steps in his direction. The caller fired another shot towards it and thinks he hit it in the chest. Stevens county employees advised they located a large cougar track in the roadway but had found no blood. Officers provided advice.

Cat approached close to two hikers. Man raised arms and yelled. Cougar hissed and swatted at the hikers. After about 5 minutes of yelling, hikers used two sprays of bear spray 15 seconds apart, then cat ran off.

Caller reported a cougar that ate several chickens the night prior. The landowner thought it was still on the property and injured. He was shown security footage of an emaciated young cougar still frequenting the property. A trap was set. The night of the 18th it had walked past the trap and the property owners father shot at it . Officers checked the trap and found no blood. Over the next two days the cougar was successfully trapped and euthanized. It was missing two of it's paws.
